data.title: Suspicious "customs fee" demand for a parcel
data.summary: A letter from "Paketzentrum Musterstadt – Zollabwicklung" claims €38.90 in import duties (Einfuhrabgaben) and handling fees are owed for a parcel (Sendungsnummer DE 4471 2290 5518) and demands payment by 9 November 2026, threatening to return or destroy the parcel otherwise. Several details in the letter strongly suggest this is a scam rather than a genuine customs notice.
data.explanation: This letter shows many classic signs of a parcel/customs scam: the payee name on the bank account does not match the sender, the IBAN fails the standard checksum check, the sender uses a reserved test email domain, contact is only offered via WhatsApp, and the sender/recipient names and address look like generic placeholders. Real German customs fees are collected by the actual carrier (e.g. Deutsche Post/DHL) or the Zollamt, never by direct bank transfer to an unrelated company under time pressure. Do not transfer any money or click any links. Instead, check directly with the courier you are actually expecting a parcel from, and consider reporting this letter as attempted fraud (e.g. to the police or Verbraucherzentrale) before doing anything else.

items.title: Do not pay without verifying – alleged customs fee
items.action: Verify independently with the actual courier/customs office whether this fee is genuine before paying anything; do not use the contact details in this letter to do so.
items.consequence: The letter claims that if no payment arrives by the stated date, the parcel will be returned to the sender or destroyed at the recipient's cost.
items.quote: Überweisen Sie 38,90 € bis 09.11.2026. Geht bis dahin keine Zahlung ein, schicken wir die Sendung an den Absender zurück oder vernichten sie kostenpflichtig.

warnings: The payee name on the bank account, "Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.", does not match the sender named on the letter, which is unusual for a legitimate customs or postal notice.
The IBAN DE96 7001 0080 0661 2345 67 fails the standard IBAN checksum validation, suggesting it is fabricated or incorrect.
The sender's email address uses the domain "clearance-mail.example", a reserved domain that is never used for genuine correspondence.
The letter insists on contact only via WhatsApp and gives a very short payment deadline, both common pressure tactics in parcel-customs scams.

Genuine German import duties are collected by the carrier (e.g. Deutsche Post/DHL) or the Zollamt, not by a separate private company demanding a bank transfer, so this letter should be treated as likely fraudulent.
